title: Banchare Danda Landfill Mapping
description: Drone surveying, photogrammetric processing, and cadastral digitisation for Kathmandu Metropolitan City, bringing a 4.9 km² orthomosaic together with distance-buffer and grid overview maps.
dataPointsRaw:
Mapped area: 4.9 km²
Client: Kathmandu Metropolitan City
Buffer distances: 300 / 450 / 900 m
Survey platform: Mavic 3 Enterprise
fullText:
I worked on the Banchare Danda landfill mapping project with Airlift Technology for the Environment Management Department of Kathmandu Metropolitan City. My responsibilities covered drone piloting, data processing, cadastral digitisation, and presenting the results to the metropolitan city.

The project brought a detailed aerial view of the landfill and its surroundings together with distance-based maps and a grid reference system. The mapped area was 4.9 km².

## My role from field to presentation

I was the drone pilot and the person in charge of data processing. After the field survey, I worked on the mapping outputs, digitised cadastral information, and presented the work to Kathmandu Metropolitan City.

- **Drone piloting:** carried out the aerial survey at the landfill site.
- **Data processing:** turned the collected imagery into usable mapping outputs.
- **Cadastral digitisation:** digitised and spatially align the supplied cadastral sheets.
- **Client presentation:** explained the outputs and spatial analysis to the metropolitan city.

## Surveying the landfill and its surroundings

Banchare Danda is a major landfill serving the Kathmandu Valley. Mapping needed to cover the wider surroundings as well as the active landfill, so the survey brief included a 1 km buffer from the site and a target image resolution of 3 cm per pixel.

The field setup used a Mavic 3 Enterprise with an RTK base station, with D-RTK3 listed among the project equipment. The aerial imagery provided the basis for the orthomosaic and the subsequent spatial work.

### From imagery to mapped information

1. **Capture:** survey the site and surrounding landscape by drone.
2. **Process:** prepare the orthomosaic from the acquired images.
3. **Integrate:** bring the cadastral material into the same spatial context.
4. **Present:** organise the outputs into maps that the client could review.

## Reading the three distance buffers

The orthomosaic shows the landfill in relation to the surrounding roads, settlement, vegetation, and terrain. Three distance buffers make that relationship easier to read on a common map.

- **300 metres:** the innermost distance boundary, shown in white.
- **450 metres:** the intermediate boundary, shown in blue.
- **900 metres:** the outer boundary, shown in coral.

These distance bands provided the framework for the cadastral overlay work and the presentation of the surrounding area.

![Orthomosaic overview of Banchare Danda with labelled 300, 450 and 900 metre buffer boundaries.](/images/banchare-danda/buffer-overview.webp)

## Cadastral work and map organisation

I digitised the supplied hardcopy cadastral sheets and aligned them with the drone orthomosaic. The work covered material from the Nuwakot and Dhading sides of the site and organised the analysis around the three distance bands.

The grid overview gave the map set a numbered reference system. It let a reviewer locate a particular part of the mapped area and connect it with the more detailed project outputs.

### Mapping structure

- **Aerial base:** a consistent orthomosaic view of the mapped area.
- **Distance layers:** the 300, 450, and 900 metre boundaries.
- **Grid references:** numbered cells for navigating the map set.
- **Coordinate reference:** WGS 1984 / UTM Zone 45N, with distances expressed in metres.

![Banchare Danda orthomosaic with numbered grid cells and a coordinate reference legend.](/images/banchare-danda/grid-overview.webp)

## Presenting the work to the metropolitan city

I presented the mapping and analysis to Kathmandu Metropolitan City. My role was to connect the field survey and processing work with a clear explanation of the finished outputs.

The orthomosaic supplied an up-to-date aerial base for the project, while the buffer and grid maps offered two ways to examine it: by distance from the landfill and by location within the map set.

## What this project brought together

The work connected field surveying, photogrammetric processing, cadastral digitisation, and communication with a municipal client. Being involved across those stages meant I could explain how the maps were produced as well as what they showed.

The resulting overview maps give the client a common spatial reference for reviewing the landfill and its surroundings.
